newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable, near-term spreads flatten.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable, near-term spreads flatten.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were steady to a little firmer in afternoon trade on Tuesday, while the half-month spread from first-half June was narrowed to flat due to ample prompt supplies, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha cargoes for both first-half June and the second-half of the month were quoted at around $209.00/210.50 per tonne.
However, inter-month spreads from first-half June onwards remained backwarded, they said.
On Monday, second-half June was sold to a South Korean trading house at $208.00.
In physical trading, several petrochemical end-users from Japan and South Korea were said to have scouted the market following a sharp decline in naphtha prices on Monday.
A major refiner bought a second-half May cargo at the mean of Japanese quotes flat for its petrochemical affiliate.
"We thought naphtha prices have come close to the rock bottom, so we decided to buy it (the second-half May cargo) before prices rebound," one trader with the refiner said.
Naphtha prices nosedived to a six-month low on Monday due to weaker crude oil prices as well as bearish regional fundamentals. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
